title: Algebraic reciprocity from finite adelic kernel and cokernel
statement:
Let $k\subset K$ be fields, let $I$ be a set, and let $(O_i)_{i\in I}$ be discrete valuation subrings of $K$ containing $k$, each with fraction field $K$ and residue field finite over $k$. Suppose that $\{i:f\notin O_i\}$ is finite for every $f\in K$. Define $P:K\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}K/O_i$ by $f\mapsto(f\bmod O_i)_i$. Assume that both $\bigcap_iO_i$ and $\operatorname{coker}P$ are finite-dimensional over $k$. For the local Tate residues defined by the finite-potent commutator construction of [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus], every $\xi\in\Omega^1_{K/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] has only finitely many nonzero residues and
$$\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{res}_{O_i}(\xi)=0.$$

source.place: Tate, §2, property R5 (sum/intersection identity), and §3, proof of Theorem 3 and its corollary, pp. 155–157: the proof uses precisely finiteness of the intersection and principal-parts cokernel. Blueprint statement: residue theorem making the cokernel trace well defined.

proof.text:
If $I=\varnothing$, the assertion is the empty sum identity, so assume $I
e\varnothing$. Define the restricted product
$$V=\{(a_i)\in\prod_i K:\{i:a_i
otin O_i\}	ext{ is finite}\},\quad A=\prod_iO_i\subset V,\quad B=\Delta K\subset V.$$
These are $k$-vector spaces. Coordinatewise multiplication makes $V$ a $K$-module: the exceptional set of $f(a_i)$ is contained in the union of the exceptional sets of $f$ and $(a_i)$, since each $O_i$ is a subring. The diagonal lies in $V$ by the assumed finite-poles condition, and it is injective since $I
e\varnothing$.

source.place: §3, proof of Theorem 3, pp. 155–156; use uncompleted copies of K in the restricted product.

proof.text:
The admissibility condition of [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] holds for $A$. Indeed, fix $f\in K$ and set $S_f=\{i:f\notin O_i\}$. Taking coordinate classes injects $(fA+A)/A$ into
$$\bigoplus_{i\in S_f}(fO_i+O_i)/O_i.$$
The kernel is zero because zero coordinate classes mean membership in $A$; the target is finite-dimensional, since $S_f$ is finite and every summand is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus]. Thus the quotient is finite-dimensional. The same argument applies to any subfamily of the coordinates. Also $B$ is $K$-stable, since $f\Delta(g)=\Delta(fg)$, so it is admissible with all these quotients zero.

source.place: §2, admissibility hypothesis of Theorem 1; §3, restricted-product lattice in the proof of Theorem 3, pp. 155–156.

proof.text: The diagonal identifies $A\cap B$ with $\bigcap_iO_i$, so $A\cap B$ is finite-dimensional. Write $D=\bigoplus_iK/O_i$ and $q:V\to D$, $q((a_i))=(a_i\bmod O_i)_i$. This is onto: choose representatives at the finitely many nonzero coordinates of an element of $D$, and choose zero elsewhere. Its kernel is $A$, and $q(\Delta f)=P(f)$. Explicitly the induced map $V/(A+B)\to D/P(K)$ has inverse sending a finitely supported family of classes to any such family of representatives modulo $A+B$: changing representatives adds an element of $A$, and changing the family by $P(f)$ adds $\Delta f$ modulo $A$. Therefore $V/(A+B)\cong\operatorname{coker}P$ is finite-dimensional.

source.place: §3, proof of Theorem 3, pp. 156–157; explicit principal-parts quotient identification with the finiteness hypothesis already assumed.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-tate-residue-lattice-identity] to $A,B\subset V$. It gives
$$\operatorname{res}_{V,A}+\operatorname{res}_{V,B}=\operatorname{res}_{V,A+B}+\operatorname{res}_{V,A\cap B}.$$
By [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus], the term for $B$ is zero because $B$ is $K$-stable; the term for $A+B$ is zero because $V/(A+B)$ is finite-dimensional; and the term for $A\cap B$ is zero because $A\cap B$ is finite-dimensional. Consequently $\operatorname{res}_{V,A}=0$ as a $k$-linear map on $\Omega^1_{K/k}$.

source.place: §3, lattice identity in the proof of Theorem 3 and its corollary, pp. 155–156.

proof.text: Fix $f,g\in K$ and put $S=\{i:f\notin O_i\}\cup\{i:g\notin O_i\}$ and $T=I\setminus S$. For $i\in T$, both $f$ and $g$ belong to $O_i$, so $f\,dg$ is the image of an element of $\Omega^1_{O_i/k}$. The annihilation clause of [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus] gives $\operatorname{res}_{O_i}(f\,dg)=0$. Hence the local residues of this elementary differential are supported in the finite set $S$.

source.place: §3, last paragraph of p. 156, using §2, R2.

proof.text:
For the finite set $S$ above write $V_T$ for the restricted product over $T$, embedded by zero on $S$, and $W_i=K$ in the $i$th coordinate for $i\in S$. Then $V=V_T\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in S}W_i$ as $K$-modules. Inside $V$ put $C_T=\prod_{i\in T}O_i$, zero on $S$, and put $C_i=O_i\subset W_i$, zero elsewhere. They are admissible by the finite-coordinate quotient calculation of step 2 and [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus]. Their sum is $A$, and each summand intersects the sum of the others in zero. Apply [lem-pc-tate-residue-lattice-identity] successively to these disjoint summands, starting with $C_T$: since [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] gives $\operatorname{res}_{V,0}=0$, induction on the finite set $S$ yields
$$\operatorname{res}_{V,A}=\operatorname{res}_{V,C_T}+\sum_{i\in S}\operatorname{res}_{V,C_i}.$$
Each containing coordinate module is $K$-stable; ambient restriction and invariance under isomorphisms in [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] identify the right side with
$$\operatorname{res}_{V_T,\prod_{i\in T}O_i}+\sum_{i\in S}\operatorname{res}_{K,O_i}.$$
This argument also covers $T=\varnothing$ and $S=\varnothing$.

source.place: §2, R1 and R5; §3, finite set S-prime decomposition in the proof of Theorem 3, p. 156.

proof.text:
Multiplication by $f$ and by $g$ preserves $\prod_{i\in T}O_i$, so its abstract residue on $f\,dg$ is zero by [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus]. For each $i\in S$, compute $\operatorname{res}_{K,O_i}$ and the local residue with the same $k$-linear projection $K\to O_i$: their commutator formulas in [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] and [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus] are both $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}([\pi m_f,m_g])$. Thus they agree on $f\,dg$. Evaluating step 6 at this differential, and using step 4, gives
$$\sum_{i\in S}\operatorname{res}_{O_i}(f\,dg)=\operatorname{res}_{V,A}(f\,dg)=0.$$
Together with step 5, this proves both assertions for $f\,dg$.

source.place: §3, proof of Theorem 3, last paragraph of p. 156; §2, formula (*) p. 152 and R2.

proof.text:
The symbol presentation in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] writes every $\xi\in\Omega^1_{K/k}$ as a finite sum $\sum_{j=1}^r f_j\,dg_j$. For each summand choose the finite support bound $S_j$ of step 5, and put $S=\bigcup_{j=1}^rS_j$. The $k$-linearity of each local residue in [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus] shows that all residues of $\xi$ outside $S$ vanish. Interchanging the two finite sums gives
$$\sum_i\operatorname{res}_{O_i}(\xi)=\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{j=1}^r\operatorname{res}_{O_i}(f_j\,dg_j)=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{i\in S_j}\operatorname{res}_{O_i}(f_j\,dg_j)=0,$$
where the last equality uses step 7. This also treats $\xi=0$ by the empty sum.

source.place: §2, symbol presentation of differentials, pp. 151–152; §3, Theorem 3 and its corollary, pp. 155–156.

split_report.blueprint: Realizes the residue-theorem clause of sk-thm-picard-duality: the sum of local Tate residues kills global differentials, making its cokernel trace well defined. New abstract nodes serve the R1/R2/R5 calculation of Tate §3.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-26e2ce539 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Tate 1968 pp.149-157 (§1 T1-T5; §2 Thm 1, (*) p.152, R1, R2, R5 p.153; §3 Thm 3 proof pp.155-156). The item's statement is unchanged against side-live. The live item is still unsplit, there is no repair note and no prior run. The 8 steps are Tate's Thm 3 proof with uncompleted K coordinates, which is valid because R1, R2 and R5 are abstract. Step-by-step: (1) V is a K-module and Δ is injective for I nonempty; (2) (fA+A)/A injects into the finite sum over i in S_f of (fO_i+O_i)/O_i, using the dvr node's quotient clause, and B=ΔK is a submodule; (3) A∩B=Δ(∩O_i) and V/(A+B)≅coker P, since q is onto with kernel A and qΔ=P; (4) R5 plus the vanishing clauses give res_{V,A}=0; (5) the dvr node's annihilation clause gives support in S; (6) the decomposition V=V_T⊕⊕W_i, R5 applied S times with res_0=0, and the ambient-restriction and isomorphism clauses; (7) R2 on C_T, and the local residue equals res_{K,O_i} because both are Tr_fp([π m_f,m_g]) for the same projection; (8) finite symbol sums and k-linearity. All hypotheses checked; the edge cases I=∅, S=∅ and T=∅ are covered. New nodes: abstract-residue-calculus (Thm 1 with (*), R1, R2) is true and was tested on A=0, A=V and finite-dimensional A. The lattice identity is exactly R5, which is non-elementary because Tr_fp is not known to be additive, and was tested on A=B, A=0, B=V and A⊂B. Both are statement-only, have 3 kinds of searches and correct blueprint.from, with no duplicates found by rg -L over dag/nodes or the blueprint. Neither restates a clause of the item or the parent, and there is no cycle. All citations are in the same unit; the Kähler definition is a Mathlib leaf; no tool_uses.
